messages:
Maria Gutierrez: Hey team, quick heads-up — my primary shift ends in ~25m (US-PST) but we just got an api surge in eu-west. I need someone to cover the EOD bridge/hand-off for the next 3 hours. Secondary (Aj) said he might be offline after 23:30 UTC. Can someone take primary until 03:00 UTC? :wave:

oncall-bot: Pager routed: INC-2026EU - high 90p latency in eu-west for hosted-generation. Pager severity: P1. Bridge: https://bridges.redwood.internal/INC-2026EU (autocreated)

ops-bot: Alert summary: error rates up 6x, token generation time > 8s 90th, increased 504s to some customers in EMEA. Related to autoscaler thrash on dedicated pools. See /metrics/dashboards/INC-2026EU

Aj Patel: I can cover shadow until 00:45 UTC but got a hard stop then (family thing). Not confident I can be primary after that. If someone can take over at 00:45 I'm happy to shadow and handoff.

Chen Li: I can take primary from 00:45->03:00 UTC if needed. Do we know the immediate mitigations? Any runbook pointers?

Maria Gutierrez: Thanks Chen — main levers right now are: scale the eu-west dedicated pool (temp upsize), enable KV cache bypass for a small percentage, and fallback routing to the cheaper-vCPU tier for non-SLA tenants. Runbook excerpt below — copying the minimal commands I used earlier.

Maria Gutierrez: ```
# Upsize dedicated pool (infra CLI)
redwood infra pool resize --region eu-west --pool dedicated-rt --gpus 8
# Enable temporary cache bypass for debug traffic only
redwood config set routing.cache_bypass=true --selector region:eu-west --percent 5
# Set fallback policy to route non-sla to cpu-tier
redwood routing set-fallback --region eu-west --target cpu-tier --threshold 95
```

Maria Gutierrez: Full runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/eu-latency-psp (steps 1-6 for quick mitigation, step 7 for postmortem notes).

Tess Nguyen: Customer impact check: which customers saw errors? Any major accounts impacted? I can notify CS if it's >2 enterprise customers.

Maria Gutierrez: Two customers with significant errors: @AcmeCorp (sync job failures, moderate) and @CliprLabs (timeouts on batch embed jobs, high). I've opened ticket tags on both. So yes, CS notify would be helpful.

Sam Barlow: I can take primary 00:45->03:00 UTC (confirmed). Will join the bridge at :00. Ping me if autoscaler thrash repeats — I'll enable stickier instance lifetimes and disable rapid scale-down.

Chen Li: Thanks Sam — I'll shadow until 01:15 and then switch to secondary. Plan: Sam primary, Chen secondary, Aj shadow until 00:45. Maria — if you can drop final notes to the bridge before you go that would be great.

Maria Gutierrez: Will do. Final notes I usually leave: active mitigations, keys changed, tickets created, customer list, and a TODO for postmortem owner. Example quick note I post to the bridge: "Mitigations applied: pool upsized to 8 GPUs, 5% cache bypass enabled, fallback routing active; CS notified for AcmeCorp & CliprLabs; PM @tess to follow up. Owning oncall: Sam Barlow (00:45-03:00 UTC)."

Aj Patel: Good plan. Leaving my terminal commands in the bridge logs, will hand over to Sam at 00:45.

oncall-bot: Reminder: add yourself to the handoff roster: /oncall handoff add --owner "Sam Barlow" --start 00:45Z --end 03:00Z --incident INC-2026EU

Tess Nguyen: I'll draft the CS note: summary + immediate customer mitigation + expected ETA to normal. Will post in #customer-notify when ready.

Maria Gutierrez: Thanks everyone. I'm logging out now — Sam, Chen, Aj: be on the bridge at :45 for the swap. If anything changes ping @here. :pray:
